reasons: Checks visible behaviour and accessibility with clear pass conditions.
Depends on a running app with specific test ids and wording.

terms.meaning: a test that drives the real app in a browser, the way a visitor would.
a tool that controls a web browser automatically for tests.
an automatic check of a page against rules that help people using screen readers and other assistive tools.
a named analyst character with its own voice in the app.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Roster page and persona checks
sections.what: Runs one browser flow for the roster page: it loads the five analysts, switches between them, and checks labels, numbers and accessibility. A second test checks a single persona page and an unknown persona.
sections.why: Likely reason: the feature needs to show that AI voices are labelled and share the same facts.
sections.watch_out: The test relies on exact wording such as AI analyst and the disclaimer, so changing those strings will break it.

summary: A browser test that checks the roster page shows five AI analysts, that picking each one changes its label but not its numbers, and that individual persona pages load or return not found.
purpose: Protects the roster feature: every analyst is visible, AI is labelled, the disclaimer is shown, the page passes accessibility checks, and unknown personas do not exist.
why: Likely reason: the app must be clear that these voices are AI, and every voice should work from the same facts. Reason not otherwise stated in the code.
how: Opens the roster page and checks the five names are visible. Selects each analyst in the switchboard and checks the label changes, the numbers stay the same, and each text is different. Checks the illustrative-example notice. Runs an accessibility scan. Opens the Iceman persona page, checks its heading, the Pressure Index, and at least two AI labels. Confirms the Hitman persona returns 404.
inputs: A running copy of the app. No user account is needed; the test is anonymous.
outputs: A pass or fail result. The test saves nothing.
risks: Many checks match exact wording such as AI analyst and the disclaimer text, so editing copy breaks the test. The number check compares every number on the page, so any change to figures breaks it.
debug: If the switchboard step fails, check the switchboard and voicing test ids on the page. If the numbers differ, compare the voicing text for each analyst. Accessibility failures list the rule ids in the failure output.
